subject: Different results when checking measurement invariance in R (measEq.syntax) and AMOS?

messages.author: ad90ef6d5432f337
messages.subject: Different results when checking measurement invariance in R (measEq.syntax) and AMOS?
parts:
Hello all!

Together with a colleague, who mainly works with Amos instead of R, we compared for our interest to what extent the same result appears in testing the measurement invariance. In R, I did the calculation with measEq.syntax from semTools.

It happened that the same result came out for metric invariance (apart from a certain rounding difference). On the level of scalar invariance, however, Amos gave one more degree of freedom, so the value for Chi² differed accordingly.

So, we calculated the same also with Mplus, where we got the same results as with R.

Our simple model for the comparison of the different statistic programs consists of six items, which load on a latent factor.


Here is the code in R:

### Measurement Model
mod.cat <- '

Informal =~ TA + ML + DF + VF + AR + SR'

### Configural Model
syntax.config <- measEq.syntax(configural.model = mod.cat,
                               data = dataG2,
                               ID.fac = "uv",
                               group = "Gender")

cat(as.character(syntax.config))

summary(syntax.config)

mod.config <- as.character(syntax.config)
fit.config <- cfa(mod.config, data = dataG2, group = "Gender")


### Metric Invariance
syntax.metric <- measEq.syntax(configural.model = mod.cat,
                   data = dataG2,
                               ID.fac = "uv",
                               group = "Gender",
                               group.equal = c("loadings"))

summary(syntax.metric)
mod.metric <- as.character(syntax.metric)
cat(mod.metric)

fit.metric <- cfa(mod.metric, data = dataG2, group = "Gender")

anova(fit.config, fit.metric)


### Scalar Invariance
syntax.scalar <- measEq.syntax(configural.model = mod.cat, data = dataG2,
                               ID.fac = "uv",
                               group = "Gender",
                               group.equal = c("loadings","intercepts"))

summary(syntax.scalar)
mod.scalar <- as.character(syntax.scalar)
cat(mod.scalar)

fit.scalar <- cfa(mod.scalar, data = dataG2, group = "Gender")
                  
anova(fit.metric, fit.scalar)

compareFit(fit.config, fit.metric, fit.scalar)

In Amos, six intercepts are equated. The model with free intercepts for the metric invariance has 23 degrees of freedom, so it seems to be logical, that with six equated intercepts six degrees of freedom are added, so in Amos there are 29 Intercepts.

InR with measEq.syntax (and also in Mplus with the function MODEL = CONFIGURAL METRIC SCALAR) there are only five degrees of freedom difference between the metric and the scalar model.

Do you have a guess where the different df (and thus, different chi² values) come from?

I would be grateful for hints!

I am guessing in Amos that the extra df occurs because the latent mean is not freed in the second group, as it is using Mplus or measEq.syntax()
